Class Base64SplittingFilter

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.filter.GenericFilterBean
org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.streaming.Base64SplittingFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter, Aware, BeanNameAware, DisposableBean, InitializingBean, EnvironmentAware, EnvironmentCapable, ServletContextAware
public class Base64SplittingFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter
Splits the document content out of a large FHIR upload before the body reaches the FHIR parser.

For Binary.data (ITI-65) and DocumentReference.content.attachment.data (ITI-105), HAPI materializes the base64 text as a String and the decoded array in Base64BinaryType, on top of the raw request bytes — several times the wire size of the document, allocated in one burst per concurrent upload. That is the one respect in which a FHIR upload is worse than an MTOM/XOP SOAP attachment, where CXF hands the application a file-backed DataHandler and nothing large ever touches the heap.

This filter restores the MTOM behavior without changing the wire format. The body is copied by a BodySplitter, which decodes the document content incrementally into a StagedContent and leaves a short marker in its place. The FHIR parser then only sees a few kilobytes of metadata, and whoever consumes the parsed resource exchanges the marker for the streamed content again — see StagedContentRegistry.forParameters(Map) and StagedContentRegistry.resolve(byte[]).

Requests below StreamingUploadOptions.engageAboveBytes() are passed through unchanged, so only large uploads take this path.

The filter must run after authentication — otherwise unauthenticated requests would be spooled to disk — and before any request logging, which then logs the slimmed-down body instead of buffering the full one.

Getting hold of the document content

Everything downstream of this filter — a HAPI resource provider, an IPF FHIR translator, a Camel route — sees a parsed resource whose Binary.data or Attachment.data is the marker, not the document. The content itself is fetched from the StagedContentRegistry of the current request, which the filter publishes as the servlet request attribute StagedContentRegistry.REQUEST_ATTRIBUTE. There are two ways in, depending on what the consumer has at hand:
  • StagedContentRegistry.forParameters(Map) — from the parameter map that a FHIR resource provider passes to a translator or route, which is the usual starting point
  • StagedContentRegistry.forRequest(jakarta.servlet.ServletRequest) — from the servlet request itself
Handing the parsed data to StagedContentRegistry.resolve(byte[]) then exchanges the marker for the StagedContent, from which the document is read as a stream: 
var content = StagedContentRegistry.forParameters(parameters)
        .flatMap(registry -> registry.resolve(binary.getData()));
if (content.isPresent()) {
    // Streams from memory or from the temporary file, whichever this document ended up in.
    DataHandler document = content.get().dataHandler(binary.getContentType());
    ...
} else {
    // Not split: binary.getData() is the document content itself.
}
Both branches have to be there. A request below StreamingUploadOptions.engageAboveBytes(), or one that arrived on a non-servlet transport, never passes this filter, so an empty Optional is the normal case rather than an error — it simply means the value in hand is already the document.

Besides the content, StagedContent also carries what was measured while the bytes streamed past: getSize() and getSha1Hex(), the latter being exactly the digest XDS expects, so a client-supplied one can be verified without a second pass over the document.

The content lives no longer than the request. The registry is closed, and any temporary file deleted, as soon as this filter returns, i.e. once the response has been produced. A consumer must therefore read the stream (or copy it somewhere it owns) while the request is being processed on the calling thread; a DataHandler handed to another thread or kept beyond the response reads from content that is already gone. Every staged document is expected to be resolved exactly once by whoever handles the request; content that is never picked up is reported as a warning, because it means the document silently did not make it into the backend request.

      public Base64SplittingFilter(StreamingUploadOptions options, FhirContext fhirContext, String fhirBasePath, UnaryOperator<String> diagnosticsPolicy, StreamedDocumentListener listener)
      Parameters:
      options - tuning parameters of the split
      fhirContext - FHIR context, used to serialize the OperationOutcome of a rejected request
      fhirBasePath - path of the FHIR endpoint below the context path, e.g. /fhir
      diagnosticsPolicy - applied to the diagnostics of a rejection before it is sent, so that an application which does not disclose error details to its clients can redact them here as well. The filter answers such requests itself and therefore bypasses whatever the FHIR servlet would have applied.
      listener - notified about every document that was streamed out of a request body
